 Appearance:
 MR HARSH R JOSHI(12752) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR HIREN M MODI(3732) for the Respondent(s) No. 2  MR MANAN MAHETA, ADDITIONAL PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the  Respondent(s) No. 1  ================================================================

sentences.text:
Learned Additional Public Prosecutor waives service of notice of Rule on behalf of the respondent-State and learned advocate Mr. Hiren M. Modi waives service of notice of Rule on behalf of respondent No.2.
2.

This application has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for quashing and setting aside the First Information Report bearing C.R. No.I-166 of 2005 registered with Visnagar Police Station, Mehsana for the offences punishable under Sections 409, 418, 420,
467, 468, 114, 477A and 120B of of the Indian Penal Code and the proceedings initiated in pursuant thereto.

sentences.text: Learned advocate for the applicant Mr. Harsh R. Joshi, submitted that the complainant-Bank had advanced finance of Rs.3,00,000/- to M.S. Traders, the applicant stood as a Guarantor for the above loan transaction.

The original borrower has repaid the outstanding amount, the account has been closed and the Bank has issued the 'No Due Certificate' in favour of the borrower (which is at Page 21 of the petition) and therefore, it is submitted the impugned complaint may be quashed and set aside.
Learned advocate submitted that the Court may verify the said aspect from the original complainant, respondent no.2.
4. Learned advocate for respondent no.2, original complainant Mr. Hiren M. Modi, concurred with the above factum advanced by learned advocate Mr. Harsh R. Joshi appearing for the applicant.

5. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor, submitted that any First Information Report should be quashed in accordance with the guidelines of the Apex Court and the parameters laid down therein and since the dispute are settled between the parties, it is submitted that necessary orders may be passed by this Court.
6.

For and on behalf of The Sarvodaya Nagarik Sahakari Bank Limited, who had given the loan to the principal borrower, Darji Ganpatbhai Ambalal who is the Liquidator of the above NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/99/2018 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined

Bank has filed an affidavit-in-reply before this Court and relevant contents of the Affidavit are as under :-
(1) I am working as Liquidator of the Sarvodaya Nagarik Sahakari Bank Ltd. (Now in Liqn.).

I have read the copy of the memo of the petition filed by the petitioner and perused the document pertaining to the application and I am duly authorized to file the present affidavit on behalf of the Respondent no.2 Bank.

(2) At the outset, I say that I am not dealing with the petition parawise and my not dealing with the petition parawise should not be construed as my admission of any of the averment made contention raised in the petition.

I deny all the averments,
allegations and contentions made by the petitioners in the petition and the same may be deemed to be specifically denied by me even if the same may not be specifically dealt with except what is expressly admitted herein.
(3) I say that the petitioner has prayed in para-13 to quash and set aside the Criminal Case No.1009 of 2015, arising out of the FIR being I-C.R. No.166 of 2005.

(4) At the outset, I say and submit that Minaxiben Patel being proprietor of M.S.
Traders obtained the loan of Rs.3,00,000/- from the Bank.
The applicant is stood as a Guarantor.
I say and submit that the loan was hypo cash credit loan, i.e. for development of business and loan is against the stocks.
The stocks were not maintained by the main borrower.

(5) It is submitted that since in connivance with the then Manager Mayankbhai Maniar, the loan was approved without any detail checking and subsequently she has Joshi Prakashkumar Navinchandra vs State Of Gujarat on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16767365/
2 not paid the loan amount.
Therefore, the impugned FIR has been lodged.
(6) I say and submit that now the loan has been repaid by the main borrower way back on 24.06.2005.

I say and submit that in such situation, being a liquidator of the Bank, I urged to pass appropriate order, this Hon'ble Court deems fit."

7. This Court has heard the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties and has perused the material on record.
This Court notices that the principal borrower after paying the amount has expired.
The role of the present petitioner is limited to the extent of being a guarantor and it would be not justified to put the present petitioner to face the trial.
The role of the present petitioner is very limited to that of being a guarantor for the loan obtained by the principal borrower.
The FIR is filed on the ground that the principal borrower did not pay the amount and as such, had siphoned off the money.
It is noticed by this Court that the principal borrower has expired.

8. In the case of State of Haryana V. Bhajan Lal and others, AIR 1992 SC 604, the Apex Court formulated as many as seven categories of cases, wherein the extraordinary power under Section 482 could be exercised by the High Court to prevent abuse of process of the court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was clarified that it was not possible to lay down precise and inflexible guidelines or any rigid formula or to give an exhaustive list of circumstances in which such power could be exercised.

In this case, the Apex Court made the following observations:-
"8.1.

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/99/2018 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined 9.
In view of the above, as well as considering the principles enunciated by the Apex Court in State of Haryana V. Bhajan Lal (supra), there exists no scope for any further proceeding in the matter.

entities.text: State of Haryana V. Bhajan Lal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The continuance of proceedings would lead to wastage of precious judicial time as there would remain no possibility of any conviction in the case.
Hence, the Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case where the inherent powers of the Court under section 482 of the Cr.P.C. could be exercised for securing the ends of justice.
10. In the result, the application is allowed.

The impugned First Information Report bearing C.R.
No.I-166 of 2005 registered with Visnagar Police Station, Mehsana and the proceedings initiated in pursuance thereof qua the applicant is quashed and set aside.
Rule is made absolute.
Direct Service is permitted.
